Two kinds of errors, two outcomes
The docs separate errors by when they happen. A command that can't be queued, such as a wrong number of arguments or an unknown command, makes Redis discard the whole transaction at
EXECABORT Transaction discarded because of previous errors.
A command that fails while running, such as
or a value that isn't an integer, is different. The docs put it in bold: "even when a command fails, all the other commands in the queue are processed".

items.text: guarantees no interleaving and that queued commands start together, not that they all succeed.
Queue-time errors discard the transaction; run-time errors don't, and the other commands still apply.
Redis has no rollback: in the test, a failed debit still let a 100-point credit through, in both a transaction and a Lua script.
